description: Dependency updates for the music-management monorepo. Every ecosystem in here (pip, npm, Gradle, Dockerfile) is picked up automatically; the rules below only decide how the updates are grouped and how eagerly they are merged.

packageRules.description: A version published minutes ago can be unpublished, yanked or found compromised in the days after, and this repository merges several ecosystems automatically. Three days is long enough for that to surface and short enough that nothing waits a week; vulnerabilityAlerts above is scheduled at any time and is not held up by it.
Patch and minor updates of the Python runtime stack move together: they are covered by the unit suite and reviewing them one by one is noise.

A major of fastapi/pydantic/sqlalchemy is a migration, not an update. It opens on its own like everything else, but never merges on its own -- no automerge rule below matches a pip major -- and the label is so it is recognisable as a migration at a glance rather than something to wave through.

yt-dlp ships breaking extractor fixes as ordinary releases; being behind on it is what actually breaks downloading. Merge automatically once the pipeline is green, and exempt it from the repo-wide cooldown -- a three-day wait here is three days of failing downloads.
Dev tooling is not shipped to production; an upgrade can only turn the pipeline red, never break a user.
Frontend dev dependencies move fast and are covered by lint + typecheck + vitest.

Frontend runtime dependencies are covered by the same gates as the dev ones -- vitest, typecheck, lint and frontend:browser all run against the built app, so a break here is a red pipeline rather than a bad deploy.
muma-mobile's dependencies live in a version catalog and move as one group; reviewing an androidx patch bump by hand is noise. Covered by muma-mobile:check.
A Gradle major is AGP, Kotlin or media3 changing its API. Labelled and left ungrouped for the same reason as the Python majors above: it opens by itself, it never merges by itself.

Test and lint libraries are not in the APK, so the worst a bad one can do is turn muma-mobile:check red -- which is the check. Majors included, for that reason.

This list is explicit rather than a match on testImplementation, and the reason is the version catalog: Renovate updates a shared version.ref, not a single coordinate. kotlin-test-junit and kotlin-reflect ride on the same `kotlin` ref as the compiler, kotlinx-coroutines-test on the runtime coroutines, and mockwebserver on okhttp. Matching those by their test-sounding names would automerge a Kotlin compiler upgrade. They stay in the runtime group above on purpose.

Base image bumps rebuild every service image, so they are reviewed by hand -- which is what an unmerged merge request already is. Nothing here automerges; the label is what makes them stand out from a library bump in the list.
Vendored upstream fork; its dependencies are managed by that project, not here.
